messages:
anas: Procurement looped me in on two proposals for invoice automation: ClearInvoice and Reconly. Pricing sheets are apples-vs-oranges. Quick sanity check please?
rachel: I ran a short sandbox with ClearInvoice earlier. Fast ingest, good mapping UI, but their pricing had a weird "reconciliation event" metric that hit us during onboarding.
ted: Can you paste the snippets? curious about min commits and whether attachments are charged.
anas: Pasted vendor excerpts below: 
```
ClearInvoice (Enterprise): $0.055 per invoice + $0.01 per attachment page. Reconciliation events (unmatched line items) $0.015/event. Min annual commit: $40k. Includes SSO, API. Onboarding: 30h included; extra PS $225/hr.
Reconly (Enterprise): $0.065 per invoice OR $0.035 + $0.0025 per extracted line-item for complex invoices. Attachments waived if ingested via S3. Min commit: $30k. Sandbox: 45 days free.
```
rachel: ClearInvoice covered OCR + header + basic line extraction in the per-invoice charge, but their reconciliation-event fee started to add up when our unmatched rate was 2-3% in early runs.
carmen: Finance constraints reminder: 1) must provide line-item-level output with tax/discount/FX fields; 2) programmatic exports (nightly S3 dump + realtime webhook); 3) audit logs per event, retained 7 years and SIEM-forwardable; 4) must accept DPA + KMS/HSM controls; 5) processing SLA: nightly batch <4h, urgent <30m.
ted: Important: how Reconly treats nested line items and whether Reconly's per-line model counts nested rows as separate lines. That can blow the budget.
anas: Procurement asked me to confirm a handful before replying. Draft questions below  please edit: 
1) Can you ingest our BigQuery export + GCS attachments? Any schema gaps?
2) Provide exact pricing formula and worked examples for invoices with 1/5/20/100 line items.
3) Does the per-invoice price include full line-item extraction (tax, discounts, FX)? If not, list per-field/line fees.
4) How are "reconciliation events" defined and billed? Are interim/unverified mismatches billed?
5) Attachments: do you charge per-page for compressed PDFs or only uncompressed? Is fee waived for S3 ingestion?
6) Do you include SSO (SAML + SCIM) and provisioning in enterprise?
7) Can GL mappings/rules be exported as JSON/YAML and version-controlled? Is rollback supported?
8) Provide a sample monthly cost model for our projected 900k invoices/yr with best/worst-case line counts and a 12/24 month schedule.
9) Provide sample SLA language for processing latency and error rate targets and remedies/credit schedule.
10) Will you sign our DPA and support KMS/HSM key control? List subprocessors.
11) Can you provide a sandbox acceptance run against our sample set and commit to a 30-day right-to-exit in year 1 if acceptance accuracy < agreed benchmark?
12) Do you expose reconciliation deltas (matched/unmatched) per webhook event and an audit feed we can forward to Splunk?

rachel: Add: ask for a sample mapped JSON for one of our redacted vendor PDFs and a CSV with line-count distribution so we can model unpredictability.
ted: negotiation levers to consider: waive reconciliation-event fees for first 90 days, include 40h PS in year 1, steep volume discounts >100k/mo, cap effective per-invoice rate (e.g., not exceed $0.05 effective), and refund/credit schedule tied to acceptance.
procurement-bot: Reminder: attach the RFP + sample BigQuery export when you reply. Use /procure/reply-template-v6.
anas: I'll send this consolidated list and paste vendor replies here. If either vendor insists on rule lock-in or refuses audit logs, it's a no-go. Sending now
